terms.gloss: edge, border; the margin of a page
evidence: Juv. 1.5: plēnā jam margine librī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The edge of anything: of a river, a pool, a shield, a wound, and of a page or a writing tablet. Masculine in most authors, feminine in Juvenal and Vitruvius. Not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short). As the edge of a road it is the kerb (see kerb).

terms.grammar: ablative of the measure of difference
evidence: M-O s.v. vote: suffrāgiīs multō plūribus ēlectus est, he was elected by a large margin
terms.comment: The margin of a win is said with the amount of the difference: multō, by much; paulō, by a little; or longē (Morgan–Owens: longē majōre suffrāgiōrum numerō).

phrases.english: Make a note in the margin.
